\DoxyCodeLine{00719\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00720\ \textcolor{comment}{3.\ Definitions}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00721\ \textcolor{comment}{==============}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00722\ \textcolor{comment}{This\ section\ defines\ common\ terms\ used\ throughout\ miniaudio.\ Unfortunately\ there\ is\ often\ ambiguity}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00723\ \textcolor{comment}{in\ the\ use\ of\ terms\ throughout\ the\ audio\ space,\ so\ this\ section\ is\ intended\ to\ clarify\ how\ miniaudio}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00724\ \textcolor{comment}{uses\ each\ term.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00725\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00726\ \textcolor{comment}{3.1.\ Sample}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00727\ \textcolor{comment}{-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00728\ \textcolor{comment}{A\ sample\ is\ a\ single\ unit\ of\ audio\ data.\ If\ the\ sample\ format\ is\ f32,\ then\ one\ sample\ is\ one\ 32-\/bit}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00729\ \textcolor{comment}{floating\ point\ number.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00730\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00731\ \textcolor{comment}{3.2.\ Frame\ /\ PCM\ Frame}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00732\ \textcolor{comment}{-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00733\ \textcolor{comment}{A\ frame\ is\ a\ group\ of\ samples\ equal\ to\ the\ number\ of\ channels.\ For\ a\ stereo\ stream\ a\ frame\ is\ 2}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00734\ \textcolor{comment}{samples,\ a\ mono\ frame\ is\ 1\ sample,\ a\ 5.1\ surround\ sound\ frame\ is\ 6\ samples,\ etc.\ The\ terms\ "{}frame"{}}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00735\ \textcolor{comment}{and\ "{}PCM\ frame"{}\ are\ the\ same\ thing\ in\ miniaudio.\ Note\ that\ this\ is\ different\ to\ a\ compressed\ frame.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00736\ \textcolor{comment}{If\ ever\ miniaudio\ needs\ to\ refer\ to\ a\ compressed\ frame,\ such\ as\ a\ FLAC\ frame,\ it\ will\ always}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00737\ \textcolor{comment}{clarify\ what\ it's\ referring\ to\ with\ something\ like\ "{}FLAC\ frame"{}.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00738\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00739\ \textcolor{comment}{3.3.\ Channel}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00740\ \textcolor{comment}{-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00741\ \textcolor{comment}{A\ stream\ of\ monaural\ audio\ that\ is\ emitted\ from\ an\ individual\ speaker\ in\ a\ speaker\ system,\ or}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00742\ \textcolor{comment}{received\ from\ an\ individual\ microphone\ in\ a\ microphone\ system.\ A\ stereo\ stream\ has\ two\ channels\ (a}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00743\ \textcolor{comment}{left\ channel,\ and\ a\ right\ channel),\ a\ 5.1\ surround\ sound\ system\ has\ 6\ channels,\ etc.\ Some\ audio}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00744\ \textcolor{comment}{systems\ refer\ to\ a\ channel\ as\ a\ complex\ audio\ stream\ that's\ mixed\ with\ other\ channels\ to\ produce}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00745\ \textcolor{comment}{the\ final\ mix\ -\/\ this\ is\ completely\ different\ to\ miniaudio's\ use\ of\ the\ term\ "{}channel"{}\ and\ should}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00746\ \textcolor{comment}{not\ be\ confused.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00747\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00748\ \textcolor{comment}{3.4.\ Sample\ Rate}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00749\ \textcolor{comment}{-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00750\ \textcolor{comment}{The\ sample\ rate\ in\ miniaudio\ is\ always\ expressed\ in\ Hz,\ such\ as\ 44100,\ 48000,\ etc.\ It's\ the\ number}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00751\ \textcolor{comment}{of\ PCM\ frames\ that\ are\ processed\ per\ second.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00752\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00753\ \textcolor{comment}{3.5.\ Formats}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00754\ \textcolor{comment}{-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00755\ \textcolor{comment}{Throughout\ miniaudio\ you\ will\ see\ references\ to\ different\ sample\ formats:}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00756\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{00757\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ +-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/+-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/+-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/+}}

\DoxyCodeLine{01951\ \textcolor{comment}{your\ file\ names\ to\ upper-\/\ or\ lower-\/case\ before\ initializing\ your\ data\ sources.\ If\ name\ collisions}}

\DoxyCodeLine{02366\ \textcolor{comment}{7.1.\ Timing}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02367\ \textcolor{comment}{-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02368\ \textcolor{comment}{The\ node\ graph\ supports\ starting\ and\ stopping\ nodes\ at\ scheduled\ times.\ This\ is\ especially\ useful}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02369\ \textcolor{comment}{for\ data\ source\ nodes\ where\ you\ want\ to\ get\ the\ node\ set\ up,\ but\ only\ start\ playback\ at\ a\ specific}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02370\ \textcolor{comment}{time.\ There\ are\ two\ clocks:\ local\ and\ global.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02371\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02372\ \textcolor{comment}{A\ local\ clock\ is\ per-\/node,\ whereas\ the\ global\ clock\ is\ per\ graph.\ Scheduling\ starts\ and\ stops\ can}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02373\ \textcolor{comment}{only\ be\ done\ based\ on\ the\ global\ clock\ because\ the\ local\ clock\ will\ not\ be\ running\ while\ the\ node}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02374\ \textcolor{comment}{is\ stopped.\ The\ global\ clocks\ advances\ whenever\ \`{}ma\_node\_graph\_read\_pcm\_frames()`\ is\ called.\ On\ the}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02375\ \textcolor{comment}{other\ hand,\ the\ local\ clock\ only\ advances\ when\ the\ node's\ processing\ callback\ is\ fired,\ and\ is}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02376\ \textcolor{comment}{advanced\ based\ on\ the\ output\ frame\ count.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02377\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02378\ \textcolor{comment}{To\ retrieve\ the\ global\ time,\ use\ \`{}ma\_node\_graph\_get\_time()`.\ The\ global\ time\ can\ be\ set\ with}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02379\ \textcolor{comment}{\`{}ma\_node\_graph\_set\_time()`\ which\ might\ be\ useful\ if\ you\ want\ to\ do\ seeking\ on\ a\ global\ timeline.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02380\ \textcolor{comment}{Getting\ and\ setting\ the\ local\ time\ is\ similar.\ Use\ \`{}ma\_node\_get\_time()`\ to\ retrieve\ the\ local\ time,}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02381\ \textcolor{comment}{and\ \`{}ma\_node\_set\_time()`\ to\ set\ the\ local\ time.\ The\ global\ and\ local\ times\ will\ be\ advanced\ by\ the}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02382\ \textcolor{comment}{audio\ thread,\ so\ care\ should\ be\ taken\ to\ avoid\ data\ races.\ Ideally\ you\ should\ avoid\ calling\ these}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02383\ \textcolor{comment}{outside\ of\ the\ node\ processing\ callbacks\ which\ are\ always\ run\ on\ the\ audio\ thread.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02384\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02385\ \textcolor{comment}{There\ is\ basic\ support\ for\ scheduling\ the\ starting\ and\ stopping\ of\ nodes.\ You\ can\ only\ schedule\ one}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02386\ \textcolor{comment}{start\ and\ one\ stop\ at\ a\ time.\ This\ is\ mainly\ intended\ for\ putting\ nodes\ into\ a\ started\ or\ stopped}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02387\ \textcolor{comment}{state\ in\ a\ frame-\/exact\ manner.\ Without\ this\ mechanism,\ starting\ and\ stopping\ of\ a\ node\ is\ limited}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02388\ \textcolor{comment}{to\ the\ resolution\ of\ a\ call\ to\ \`{}ma\_node\_graph\_read\_pcm\_frames()`\ which\ would\ typically\ be\ in\ blocks}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02389\ \textcolor{comment}{of\ several\ milliseconds.\ The\ following\ APIs\ can\ be\ used\ for\ scheduling\ node\ states:}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02390\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02391\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ \`{}\`{}\`{}c}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02392\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ ma\_node\_set\_state\_time()}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02393\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ ma\_node\_get\_state\_time()}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02394\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ \`{}\`{}\`{}}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02395\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02396\ \textcolor{comment}{The\ time\ is\ absolute\ and\ must\ be\ based\ on\ the\ global\ clock.\ An\ example\ is\ below:}}

\DoxyCodeLine{02399\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ ma\_node\_set\_state\_time(\&myNode,\ ma\_node\_state\_started,\ sampleRate*1);\ \ \ //\ Delay\ starting\ to\ 1\ second.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02400\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ ma\_node\_set\_state\_time(\&myNode,\ ma\_node\_state\_stopped,\ sampleRate*5);\ \ \ //\ Delay\ stopping\ to\ 5\ seconds.}}

\DoxyCodeLine{02402\ \textcolor{comment}{}}

\DoxyCodeLine{02405\ \textcolor{comment}{\ \ \ \ \`{}\`{}\`{}c}}

\DoxyCodeLine{02417\ \textcolor{comment}{7.2.\ Thread\ Safety\ and\ Locking}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02418\ \textcolor{comment}{-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02419\ \textcolor{comment}{When\ processing\ audio,\ it's\ ideal\ not\ to\ have\ any\ kind\ of\ locking\ in\ the\ audio\ thread.\ Since\ it's}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02420\ \textcolor{comment}{expected\ that\ \`{}ma\_node\_graph\_read\_pcm\_frames()`\ would\ be\ run\ on\ the\ audio\ thread,\ it\ does\ so}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02421\ \textcolor{comment}{without\ the\ use\ of\ any\ locks.\ This\ section\ discusses\ the\ implementation\ used\ by\ miniaudio\ and\ goes}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02422\ \textcolor{comment}{over\ some\ of\ the\ compromises\ employed\ by\ miniaudio\ to\ achieve\ this\ goal.\ Note\ that\ the\ current}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02423\ \textcolor{comment}{implementation\ may\ not\ be\ ideal\ -\/\ feedback\ and\ critiques\ are\ most\ welcome.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02424\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02425\ \textcolor{comment}{The\ node\ graph\ API\ is\ not\ *entirely*\ lock-\/free.\ Only\ \`{}ma\_node\_graph\_read\_pcm\_frames()`\ is\ expected}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02426\ \textcolor{comment}{to\ be\ lock-\/free.\ Attachment,\ detachment\ and\ uninitialization\ of\ nodes\ use\ locks\ to\ simplify\ the}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02427\ \textcolor{comment}{implementation,\ but\ are\ crafted\ in\ a\ way\ such\ that\ such\ locking\ is\ not\ required\ when\ reading\ audio}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02428\ \textcolor{comment}{data\ from\ the\ graph.\ Locking\ in\ these\ areas\ are\ achieved\ by\ means\ of\ spinlocks.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02429\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02430\ \textcolor{comment}{The\ main\ complication\ with\ keeping\ \`{}ma\_node\_graph\_read\_pcm\_frames()`\ lock-\/free\ stems\ from\ the\ fact}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02431\ \textcolor{comment}{that\ a\ node\ can\ be\ uninitialized,\ and\ it's\ memory\ potentially\ freed,\ while\ in\ the\ middle\ of\ being}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02432\ \textcolor{comment}{processed\ on\ the\ audio\ thread.\ There\ are\ times\ when\ the\ audio\ thread\ will\ be\ referencing\ a\ node,}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02433\ \textcolor{comment}{which\ means\ the\ uninitialization\ process\ of\ a\ node\ needs\ to\ make\ sure\ it\ delays\ returning\ until\ the}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02434\ \textcolor{comment}{audio\ thread\ is\ finished\ so\ that\ control\ is\ not\ handed\ back\ to\ the\ caller\ thereby\ giving\ them\ a}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02435\ \textcolor{comment}{chance\ to\ free\ the\ node's\ memory.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02436\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02437\ \textcolor{comment}{When\ the\ audio\ thread\ is\ processing\ a\ node,\ it\ does\ so\ by\ reading\ from\ each\ of\ the\ output\ buses\ of}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02438\ \textcolor{comment}{the\ node.\ In\ order\ for\ a\ node\ to\ process\ data\ for\ one\ of\ its\ output\ buses,\ it\ needs\ to\ read\ from}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02439\ \textcolor{comment}{each\ of\ its\ input\ buses,\ and\ so\ on\ an\ so\ forth.\ It\ follows\ that\ once\ all\ output\ buses\ of\ a\ node}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02440\ \textcolor{comment}{are\ detached,\ the\ node\ as\ a\ whole\ will\ be\ disconnected\ and\ no\ further\ processing\ will\ occur\ unless}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02441\ \textcolor{comment}{it's\ output\ buses\ are\ reattached,\ which\ won't\ be\ happening\ when\ the\ node\ is\ being\ uninitialized.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02442\ \textcolor{comment}{By\ having\ \`{}ma\_node\_detach\_output\_bus()`\ wait\ until\ the\ audio\ thread\ is\ finished\ with\ it,\ we\ can}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02443\ \textcolor{comment}{simplify\ a\ few\ things,\ at\ the\ expense\ of\ making\ \`{}ma\_node\_detach\_output\_bus()`\ a\ bit\ slower.\ By}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02444\ \textcolor{comment}{doing\ this,\ the\ implementation\ of\ \`{}ma\_node\_uninit()`\ becomes\ trivial\ -\/\ just\ detach\ all\ output}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02445\ \textcolor{comment}{nodes,\ followed\ by\ each\ of\ the\ attachments\ to\ each\ of\ its\ input\ nodes,\ and\ then\ do\ any\ final\ clean}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02446\ \textcolor{comment}{up.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02447\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02448\ \textcolor{comment}{With\ the\ above\ design,\ the\ worst-\/case\ scenario\ is\ \`{}ma\_node\_detach\_output\_bus()`\ taking\ as\ long\ as}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02449\ \textcolor{comment}{it\ takes\ to\ process\ the\ output\ bus\ being\ detached.\ This\ will\ happen\ if\ it's\ called\ at\ just\ the}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02450\ \textcolor{comment}{wrong\ moment\ where\ the\ audio\ thread\ has\ just\ iterated\ it\ and\ has\ just\ started\ processing.\ The}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02451\ \textcolor{comment}{caller\ of\ \`{}ma\_node\_detach\_output\_bus()`\ will\ stall\ until\ the\ audio\ thread\ is\ finished,\ which}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02452\ \textcolor{comment}{includes\ the\ cost\ of\ recursively\ processing\ its\ inputs.\ This\ is\ the\ biggest\ compromise\ made\ with}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02453\ \textcolor{comment}{the\ approach\ taken\ by\ miniaudio\ for\ its\ lock-\/free\ processing\ system.\ The\ cost\ of\ detaching\ nodes}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02454\ \textcolor{comment}{earlier\ in\ the\ pipeline\ (data\ sources,\ for\ example)\ will\ be\ cheaper\ than\ the\ cost\ of\ detaching}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02455\ \textcolor{comment}{higher\ level\ nodes,\ such\ as\ some\ kind\ of\ final\ post-\/processing\ endpoint.\ If\ you\ need\ to\ do\ mass}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02456\ \textcolor{comment}{detachments,\ detach\ starting\ from\ the\ lowest\ level\ nodes\ and\ work\ your\ way\ towards\ the\ final}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02457\ \textcolor{comment}{endpoint\ node\ (but\ don't\ try\ detaching\ the\ node\ graph's\ endpoint).\ If\ the\ audio\ thread\ is\ not}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02458\ \textcolor{comment}{running,\ detachment\ will\ be\ fast\ and\ detachment\ in\ any\ order\ will\ be\ the\ same.\ The\ reason\ nodes}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02459\ \textcolor{comment}{need\ to\ wait\ for\ their\ input\ attachments\ to\ complete\ is\ due\ to\ the\ potential\ for\ desyncs\ between}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02460\ \textcolor{comment}{data\ sources.\ If\ the\ node\ was\ to\ terminate\ processing\ mid\ way\ through\ processing\ its\ inputs,}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02461\ \textcolor{comment}{there's\ a\ chance\ that\ some\ of\ the\ underlying\ data\ sources\ will\ have\ been\ read,\ but\ then\ others\ not.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02462\ \textcolor{comment}{That\ will\ then\ result\ in\ a\ potential\ desynchronization\ when\ detaching\ and\ reattaching\ higher-\/level}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02463\ \textcolor{comment}{nodes.\ A\ possible\ solution\ to\ this\ is\ to\ have\ an\ option\ when\ detaching\ to\ terminate\ processing}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02464\ \textcolor{comment}{before\ processing\ all\ input\ attachments\ which\ should\ be\ fairly\ simple.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02465\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02466\ \textcolor{comment}{Another\ compromise,\ albeit\ less\ significant,\ is\ locking\ when\ attaching\ and\ detaching\ nodes.\ This}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02467\ \textcolor{comment}{locking\ is\ achieved\ by\ means\ of\ a\ spinlock\ in\ order\ to\ reduce\ memory\ overhead.\ A\ lock\ is\ present}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02468\ \textcolor{comment}{for\ each\ input\ bus\ and\ output\ bus.\ When\ an\ output\ bus\ is\ connected\ to\ an\ input\ bus,\ both\ the\ output}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02469\ \textcolor{comment}{bus\ and\ input\ bus\ is\ locked.\ This\ locking\ is\ specifically\ for\ attaching\ and\ detaching\ across}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02470\ \textcolor{comment}{different\ threads\ and\ does\ not\ affect\ \`{}ma\_node\_graph\_read\_pcm\_frames()`\ in\ any\ way.\ The\ locking\ and}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02471\ \textcolor{comment}{unlocking\ is\ mostly\ self-\/explanatory,\ but\ a\ slightly\ less\ intuitive\ aspect\ comes\ into\ it\ when}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02472\ \textcolor{comment}{considering\ that\ iterating\ over\ attachments\ must\ not\ break\ as\ a\ result\ of\ attaching\ or\ detaching\ a}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02473\ \textcolor{comment}{node\ while\ iteration\ is\ occurring.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02474\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02475\ \textcolor{comment}{Attaching\ and\ detaching\ are\ both\ quite\ simple.\ When\ an\ output\ bus\ of\ a\ node\ is\ attached\ to\ an\ input}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02476\ \textcolor{comment}{bus\ of\ another\ node,\ it's\ added\ to\ a\ linked\ list.\ Basically,\ an\ input\ bus\ is\ a\ linked\ list,\ where}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02477\ \textcolor{comment}{each\ item\ in\ the\ list\ is\ and\ output\ bus.\ We\ have\ some\ intentional\ (and\ convenient)\ restrictions\ on}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02478\ \textcolor{comment}{what\ can\ done\ with\ the\ linked\ list\ in\ order\ to\ simplify\ the\ implementation.\ First\ of\ all,\ whenever}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02479\ \textcolor{comment}{something\ needs\ to\ iterate\ over\ the\ list,\ it\ must\ do\ so\ in\ a\ forward\ direction.\ Backwards\ iteration}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02480\ \textcolor{comment}{is\ not\ supported.\ Also,\ items\ can\ only\ be\ added\ to\ the\ start\ of\ the\ list.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02481\ \textcolor{comment}{}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02482\ \textcolor{comment}{The\ linked\ list\ is\ a\ doubly-\/linked\ list\ where\ each\ item\ in\ the\ list\ (an\ output\ bus)\ holds\ a\ pointer}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02483\ \textcolor{comment}{to\ the\ next\ item\ in\ the\ list,\ and\ another\ to\ the\ previous\ item.\ A\ pointer\ to\ the\ previous\ item\ is}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02484\ \textcolor{comment}{only\ required\ for\ fast\ detachment\ of\ the\ node\ -\/\ it\ is\ never\ used\ in\ iteration.\ This\ is\ an}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02485\ \textcolor{comment}{important\ property\ because\ it\ means\ from\ the\ perspective\ of\ iteration,\ attaching\ and\ detaching\ of}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02486\ \textcolor{comment}{an\ item\ can\ be\ done\ with\ a\ single\ atomic\ assignment.\ This\ is\ exploited\ by\ both\ the\ attachment\ and}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02487\ \textcolor{comment}{detachment\ process.\ When\ attaching\ the\ node,\ the\ first\ thing\ that\ is\ done\ is\ the\ setting\ of\ the}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02488\ \textcolor{comment}{local\ "{}next"{}\ and\ "{}previous"{}\ pointers\ of\ the\ node.\ After\ that,\ the\ item\ is\ "{}attached"{}\ to\ the\ list}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02489\ \textcolor{comment}{by\ simply\ performing\ an\ atomic\ exchange\ with\ the\ head\ pointer.\ After\ that,\ the\ node\ is\ "{}attached"{}}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02490\ \textcolor{comment}{to\ the\ list\ from\ the\ perspective\ of\ iteration.\ Even\ though\ the\ "{}previous"{}\ pointer\ of\ the\ next\ item}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02491\ \textcolor{comment}{hasn't\ yet\ been\ set,\ from\ the\ perspective\ of\ iteration\ it's\ been\ attached\ because\ iteration\ will}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02492\ \textcolor{comment}{only\ be\ happening\ in\ a\ forward\ direction\ which\ means\ the\ "{}previous"{}\ pointer\ won't\ actually\ ever\ get}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02493\ \textcolor{comment}{used.\ The\ same\ general\ process\ applies\ to\ detachment.\ See\ \`{}ma\_node\_attach\_output\_bus()`\ and}}
\DoxyCodeLine{02494\ \textcolor{comment}{\`{}ma\_node\_detach\_output\_bus()`\ for\ the\ implementation\ of\ this\ mechanism.}}
